summary: Sustained mass-balance deficit of 0.52 MMSCFD detected at ST-05 beginning 2026-01-04T23:55. Pressure dropped from 755.13 to 750.24 PSI with deficit increasing to 0.74 MMSCFD over the following 20 minutes. No compressor start, valve change, or temperature transient explains the anomaly. Classified as real leak per operating procedure transient evaluation criteria.

observations.label: Mass balance deficit onset
observations.value: 0.02 MMSCFD rising to 0.69 MMSCFD within 5 minutes

alternatives_considered.reason: ST-05 compressor remained in standby throughout the investigation window. No compressor start event logged.
Valve position at ST-05 remained within normal operating range (80–89%). No step change detected.
Gas temperature at ST-05 was 39.0–43.6°F with no sudden drop. Ambient temperature stable per weather data. Insufficient temperature movement to explain sustained deficit.

recommended_actions.action: Dispatch field verification crew to mile marker 119 ± 2 miles on SEG-05
recommended_actions.basis: Pipeline Operating Procedures — pressure anomaly response

recommended_actions.action: Prepare isolation of SEG-05 via valves V-112 (mile 112) and V-122 (mile 122)
recommended_actions.basis: Pipeline Operating Procedures — isolation valve procedures; leak rate 0.52 MMSCFD exceeds 0.3 MMSCFD isolation threshold

recommended_actions.action: Monitor cumulative gas release — at 0.52 MMSCFD, the 3 MMSCF PHMSA reporting threshold is reached in approximately 5.8 days
recommended_actions.basis: 49 CFR 191.5 — NRC notification required within 1 hour of confirmed reportable release

citations.claim: Pressure dropped from 755.13 to 750.24 PSI at onset; mass balance deficit rose from 0.02 to 0.74 MMSCFD and persisted
Confirmed leak at mile 119.3 on SEG-05, leak rate 0.52 MMSCFD, severity moderate
Segment spans ST-05 to ST-06, 26 miles, isolation valves at mile 112 and 122
ILI UT inspection found dent anomaly with 86.1% wall-loss depth — elevated integrity risk
Sustained deficit with no operational cause requires field verification and isolation preparation
Releases exceeding 3 MMSCF cumulative require NRC notification within 1 hour
